result: I would remove humanity's instinct to treat uncertainty as an enemy. Not by eliminating unpredictability, but by rewiring the default response to it. If people could naturally sit with ambiguity, hold competing truths without demanding immediate certainty, and make choices based on long-term patterns instead of short-term fear, nearly every systemic fracture would lose its fuel. Borders would soften. Institutions would adapt. Violence would lose its shortcut appeal. The world wouldn't become utopian, but it would become navigable. And navigable is where actual progress lives.
